summary: The candidate is a narrow, source-level fix for both reported defects. On the exact base, its regression fails for the disabled-pynccl eager path and for missing pre-profile symmetric allocation; at the exact candidate commit it passes with the existing DCP layout suite. Independent cases confirmed communicator state restoration on transport exceptions and correct early-call arguments for disabled symmetric memory and draft workers. Acceptance is recommended on code and regression evidence, while full resolution of the original CUDA/NCCL TP=8/DCP=8 concurrency-64 incident remains unverified on the assigned single AMD GPU.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before control flow: 2 failed, 2 passed. Disabled pynccl fell through to torch.distributed and pre-profile symmetric reservation was absent.
Candidate regression and existing DCP layout coverage: 21 passed and 18 subtests passed.

Four independent adversarial cases passed: old enabled/disabled state is restored after a pynccl transport exception, and early reservation receives the correct disabled-feature and draft-worker guards before profiling.
All changed Python source and the regression compile successfully.
Imports resolved to /job/repo/python/sglang; torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 reported one AMD Instinct MI350X, capability (9, 5), and GPU sum-of-squares 10416 matched an independent CPU reference.

gpu_execution_evidence: A simple numerical probe executed on the sole assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) and matched the CPU reference. It did not exercise multi-rank DCP or CUDA/NCCL.
remaining_counterexamples: The exact TP=8/DCP=8, concurrency-64 eager-decode workload on CUDA with NCCL 2.27.7 was not executable on the single-GPU ROCm host, so the reported pyncclGroupEnd crash is not end-to-end disproved.

The 4 GiB symmetric-memory allocation and real KV-cache budget were not exercised with the reporter's model weights, so startup OOM avoidance is established by ordering/control-flow evidence rather than a full model launch.
remaining_limitations: Only one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) was available; the report requires eight CUDA GPUs.
The environment uses ROCm 7.2/RCCL rather than CUDA/NCCL 2.27.7.
No model weights were available, and no semantic, full-serving, or multi-node claim is made.
The candidate changes Python only; no native library changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
